text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has asked ministries and government offices to proceed immediately with a plan to move the flash flood-prone Lai Chau provincial town and neighbouring Muong Lay district town to other locations.

-- As foreign direct investment decreases in big cities like Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City and Dong Nai, there are signs that it is growing in the provinces. Total investment in Hanoi this year has been over $500 million and in Ho Chi Minh City about $1.0 billion, a reduction of about 50 percent from the same period of last year.

-- The Vietnan Post and Telecommunications Corporation (VNPT) is expected to lower the cost of international telephone calls from early next year. A VNPT official, who said the price reduction would be the corporation's sixth since 1991, declined to say how far rates would be cut.
-- Vietnam has for the first time attended a meeting of the organisation set up in 1981 to promote trade, investment and tourism between Japan and ASEAN, but only as an observer.
-- Vietnam should stop importing facing stone as soon as possible, Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi said.

-- More than 320 foreign investment projects with total capital of $5.18 billion were licensed between January 1 and December 7. The total is expected to rise to $7-7.5 billion by the end of the year.
-- The Philippines' President Fidel Ramos told Vietnam's ambassador in Manila that be believed relations of friendship between the two countries would continue to develop.
-- More than 4,900 corruption cases, causing losses of about $145.27 million, were uncovered between January 1993 and September 1996.
-- State budget revenue for the whole year is expected to fall short of plans, reaching 96.9 percent of the targetted amount.
